source_title: Antrim Senior Hurling Championship: Dual demands have tested Dunloy before final - Shane Elliott - BBC
source_excerpt:
Dunloy forward Keelan Molloy scored an early goal in their semi-final victory over Glenariffe
Dunloy manager Shane Elliott admits balancing the demands of Gaelic football and hurling has proved difficult as his side prepare to face Cushendall in the Antrim Senior Hurling Championship final.
The Cuchullains are bidding to reclaim the county title after missing out on the decider last year, with a dominant 5-21 to 0-6 semi-final victory over Glenariffe securing their return to Sunday's refixed showpiece at McQuillan Park in Ballycastle.
Dunloy ended an 89-year wait to win the Antrim Senior Football Championship last year, but their title defence ended in the semi-finals this season, allowing their dual players to turn their full attention to hurling.
"It's far from easy," Elliott told BBC Sport NI's Mark Sidebottom.
"As in football management and Hurling, we work very closely together to try and manage the load of the players, so that comes with its own problems, and keeping everybody fit, and having everybody coming in at the right time.
"We would both want more access to the players at certain times, but we have to compromise on both sides to keep the show on the road.
"County finals are never easy, but this is exactly where we wanted to be. We were massively disappointed with how last year ended, so we made it our mission to make it back to the final."
'Football defeat was a kick in the teeth'
Dunloy forward Keelan Molloy, who scored an early goal in their semi-final victory over Glenariffe, echoed his manager's assessment of the challenges facing the club's dual players.
"You're week in, week out, and any chance you can get to get a break, a week off, it's everything for us," Molloy said.
"Getting beat in football was a real kick in the teeth, but we couldn't linger on it too much because we knew we had the hurling to focus back on."
Glenariffe had produced one of the shocks of the championship by eliminating defending champions St John's in the quarter-finals, but Dunloy made a blistering start to their last-four encounter.
"I just didn't expect to get a chance like that that early, so when I took it I thought, right, we've started well here, we're on it," Molloy said.
"We put a lot of focus into Glenariffe, we gave them the respect that they deserve, because they have improved during the championship."
Elliott also has injury concerns, with Antrim hurler Eoin O'Neill a "massive doubt" because of a shoulder injury, while full-back Darren McMullan has also required treatment.
Dual star Keelan Molloy is chasing hurling honours after Dunloy's football defence was ended in the semi-finals
Molloy, meanwhile, admits Cushendall will be weakened by the absence of experienced defender Paddy Burke, who is recovering from hip surgery.
"Paddy's a great player. His brother's not far behind him now; I had him in the group stage, and they're definitely cut from the same cloth," Molloy said.
"It's definitely a bit of an advantage for us, him not being there."
Dunloy will be hoping to repeat their group-stage victory over Cushendall, although Elliott acknowledges the familiarity between the sides leaves little room for surprises.
"We've played them already in the group stages this year, so we've had a good look at Cushendall, as they will have had a good look at us," he said.
"They know our players as well as we know their players, we know their strengths, we will look at where we think they may have some weaknesses that we can exploit.
"We know with Cushendall, they know how to win championships, so do we, so it makes for a very, very interesting final."

## मैच का पूर्वावलोकन
- **तारीख और स्थल:** रविवार, शाम 7 बजे (GMT) – मैकक्विलन पार्क, बैलीकासल।
- **टीमें:** डनलोई (कुचुल्लैन) बनाम कुशेंडॉल।
- **प्रतियोगिता:** एंट्रिम सीनियर हर्लिंग चैंपियनशिप फाइनल, सेमी‑फ़ाइनल के बाद पुनर्निर्धारित।
- **पिछला सामना:** इस सीज़न की ग्रुप स्टेज में डनलोई ने कुशेंडॉल को हराया था।

## दोहरी कोड की माँगें
डनलोई के मैनेजर **शेन एलेयट** ने बीबीसी स्पोर्ट एनआई को बताया कि गैलिक फुटबॉल और हर्लिंग दोनों को साथ‑साथ चलाना “बहुत आसान नहीं” है।  क्लब के दोहरे खिलाड़ी कोचिंग, मेडिकल मॉनिटरिंग और मैच तैयारी में दोनों खेलों के बीच समय बाँटना पड़ता है।  एलेयट ने कहा:
> “फुटबॉल मैनेजमेंट और हर्लिंग दोनों में हम खिलाड़ियों के लोड को मैनेज करने के लिए बहुत करीब से काम करते हैं… हम दोनों ही कुछ समय पर खिलाड़ियों तक अधिक पहुँच चाहते हैं, लेकिन हमें दोनों पक्षों में समझौता करना पड़ता है ताकि खेल जारी रह सके।”

## खिलाड़ियों की राय
फ़ॉरवर्ड **कीलन मोल्लोय** ने मैनेजर की बात दोहराई:
> “हफ़्ते‑हफ़्ते की बात है, और जब भी हमें एक हफ़्ता आराम मिल जाए, वह हमारे लिए सब कुछ है। फुटबॉल में हार एक किक‑इन‑द‑टूथ जैसा था, लेकिन हम उस पर ज़्यादा समय नहीं बिता सके क्योंकि हमें पता था कि अब हर्लिंग पर ध्यान देना है।”
मोल्लोय ने यह भी बताया कि कुशेंडॉल को अनुभवी डिफेंडर **पैडी बर्क** की कमी होगी, जो हिप सर्जरी से ठीक हो रहे हैं।

## चोट‑संबंधी अपडेट
- **ईओन ओ’नील (एंट्रिम हर्लर)** – कंधे की चोट के कारण “बहुत बड़ा संदेह”।
- **डैरेन मैकमुलन (फुल‑बैक)** – अनिर्दिष्ट समस्या के कारण उपचार चल रहा है।

## ध्यान देने योग्य बातें
- **दोहरी खिलाड़ियों की फिटनेस** – फुटबॉल सेमी‑फ़ाइनल हार के बाद उनका पुनःस्थापन कैसे हुआ।
- **कुशेंडॉल की रक्षा** – पैडी बर्क की अनुपस्थिति का असर।
- **रणनीतिक परिचितता** – दोनों टीमों ने पहले ही ग्रुप स्टेज में एक‑दूसरे को अच्छी तरह पढ़ लिया है, इसलिए आश्चर्यजनक रणनीति कम हो सकती है।

## व्यावहारिक निहितार्थ
- दर्शकों को एक कड़ी प्रतिस्पर्धा की उम्मीद करनी चाहिए, जहाँ दोनों पक्ष अपनी सबसे फिट लाइन‑अप पेश करेंगे।
- इस फाइनल का परिणाम एंट्रिम के अन्य क्लबों के दोहरी‑कोड खिलाड़ियों के प्रबंधन पर असर डाल सकता है।

## सत्यापन कैसे करें
उपरोक्त जानकारी बीबीसी स्पोर्ट के शेन एलेयट और कीलन मोल्लोय के साक्षात्कार (4 अक्टूबर 2024) से ली गई है।  एंट्रिम जीएए की आधिकारिक वेबसाइट और फाइनल का मैच‑प्रोग्राम तारीख, स्थल और टीम सूची की पुष्टि करते हैं।
hi_title: डनलोई की दोहरी खेल चुनौती: कुशेंडॉल के खिलाफ एंट्रिम हर्लिंग फाइनल

## Match preview
- **Date & venue:** Sunday, 7 pm (GMT) – McQuillan Park, Ballycastle.
- **Teams:** Dunloy (the Cuchullains) vs Cushendall.
- **Competition:** Antrim Senior Hurling Championship final, a refixed showpiece after the semi‑finals.
- **Last meeting:** Dunloy beat Cushendall in the group stage earlier this season.

## Dual‑code demands
Dunloy manager **Shane Elliott** told BBC Sport NI that juggling Gaelic football and hurling has been “far from easy”.  The club’s dual players must split training time, medical monitoring and match preparation between the two codes.  Elliott said:
> “As in football management and hurling, we work very closely together to try and manage the load of the players… we would both want more access to the players at certain times, but we have to compromise on both sides to keep the show on the road.”

## Player insights
Forward **Keelan Molloy** echoed the manager’s view:
> “You’re week in, week out, and any chance you can get a break, a week off, it’s everything for us. Getting beat in football was a real kick in the teeth, but we couldn’t linger on it too much because we knew we had the hurling to focus back on.”
Molloy also noted that Cushendall will miss experienced defender **Paddy Burke**, who is recovering from hip surgery.

## Injury updates
- **Eoin O’Neill (Antrim hurler)** – listed as a “massive doubt” with a shoulder injury.
- **Darren McMullan (full‑back)** – undergoing treatment for an unspecified issue.

## What to watch
- **Fitness of dual players** – how well the club has balanced recovery after the football semi‑final loss.
- **Cushendall’s defence** – the impact of Paddy Burke’s absence.
- **Tactical familiarity** – both sides have already studied each other from the group stage, so surprise tactics may be limited.

## Practical implications
- Supporters should expect a tightly contested final with both squads fielding their strongest available line‑ups.
- The outcome could influence how other Antrim clubs manage dual‑code athletes in future seasons.

## How to verify
The details above are drawn from the BBC Sport interview with Shane Elliott and Keelan Molloy (published 4 Oct 2024).  The official Antrim GAA website and the match programme for the final confirm the date, venue and team line‑ups.
